courseTitle: How IT Teams Work: Agile, Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban & Software Releases

slots.practicalActivity: Watch both lessons, then write a one-paragraph comparison of Agile vs. Waterfall in your own words. Imagine you're a new data engineer asked to 'add a daily refresh for the regional sales numbers in our Snowflake warehouse' -- write 3 sample user stories ("As a ___, I want ___, so that ___") breaking that request into backlog-sized pieces, each with one acceptance criterion, sized to fit in a single 2-week sprint.
slots.deliverable: A written Agile-vs-Waterfall comparison paragraph, plus 3 sprint-ready user stories for a Snowflake data-refresh request, each with an acceptance criterion.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a simple Kanban board (a free tool like Trello, or a 4-column table on paper) with To Do / In Progress / Review / Done, and place the 3 user stories from the previous hour on it. Then write, for each story, which SDLC environment (Dev, QA, UAT, Production) a data engineer's change would move through -- e.g. building and testing a new Snowflake view in a dev database before it's ever pointed at by a production dashboard.
slots.deliverable: A populated Kanban board with the 3 user stories, plus a written Dev -> QA -> UAT -> Production path for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a free GitHub account if you don't already have one. Initialize a practice repository, add a folder of .sql files representing Snowflake view/table definitions, make at least 3 commits with clear, descriptive commit messages, and open one pull request against a second branch. Then write a short explanation of 2-3 checks a CI/CD pipeline would typically run automatically against those SQL files before the pull request is allowed to merge (e.g. a linter, a dry-run against a dev schema).
slots.deliverable: A GitHub repository link with 3+ real commits and 1 pull request containing sample SQL files, plus a written explanation of what a CI/CD pipeline would check before merging them.

slots.practicalActivity: Complete the Real-World IT Project Simulation lesson's full checklist: write the user stories for the sales director's dashboard request, build the Kanban board, write a QA test plan (including the zero-sales edge case), write a one-paragraph UAT sign-off in the sales director's voice, write short specific release notes, and write up how you'd investigate a production incident where a region's numbers show as zero after launch. Then write a half-page reflection connecting Agile/Scrum, Kanban, Git, and CI/CD to each step of the simulation -- and note specifically where, in a real data warehouse like the ones you'll build in Snowflake, a bad data refresh could cause that same zero-sales incident.
slots.deliverable: The completed simulation checklist (stories, board, test plan, UAT sign-off, release notes, incident response), plus a written reflection tying Agile, Kanban, Git, and CI/CD to each step and to a realistic data-warehouse failure mode.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: Can explain Agile vs. Waterfall and Scrum/Kanban in plain language, has made real commits and opened a pull request on GitHub, and has walked one business request end to end through user stories, a Kanban board, QA/UAT, release notes, and a production incident response -- the shared professional vocabulary every data-engineering team expects on day one.
